text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--The left-wing opposition Socialist Peoples Party is deeply split over the Amsterdam Treaty after leader Holger Nielsen announced that he was leaning towards recommending a 'no' to the EU reforms in Denmark's referendum to be held in 1998. The party's European affairs spokesman says he is willing to resign in the event of a 'no', while the rejectionists are calling for 'yes' advocates, who include leading party figures, to quit.

--Former Danish EU budget commissioner Henning Christophersen warns that a Danish 'no' to Amsterdam in the national referendum to be held at an as yet unspecified date next year would mean Denmark's exit from the European Union.

--The building of private housing in Denmark is at present going on at the fastest pace in the past decade with 6,600 detached units going up this year, rising to an estimated 7,100 in 1998, the Danish building contractors' association says in a report.

--Denmark's meat industry fears reduced prices for beef after EU Commission disclosures of illegal exports of unspecified quantities of British beef to European Union and other countries in defiance of an EU ban imposed after the British government said it was possible a human form of the fatal mad cow disease, CJD, could be caught from eating infected beef.
